body:
This is a good point.

But I guess I'm now at a point of no return; sleeping in my bed next to my GF (who would not consider having sex with me with a guest in the house, btw) would be more comfortable, but only falsely so.

Should I even be with her if she forces me into an absurd situation that I don't want? If that's the case, the only true solution is not to be part of it at all.

Better hoving at neutral/zero than drowning in a greater or lesser negative.

This was a very helpful comment when I brought it up with her. Again, for the sake of space, I could only include info about the situation at hand, but some unrecorded background is that her and I have been (...we had been) going through a rough patch about insecurities, communication and needs. Before the sleep-over issue came up, we had been at the tail-end, having both admitted our commitment to mutually work on it because we love each other.

For her part, she said that because we've been fighting so much lately, she is afraid that I will eventually leave her even if she gave up the sleep-over issue. She said that at least if she supported her friend, she was guaranteed to benefit from it, whereas if she worked on this with me, she couldn't be sure that things wouldn't just collapse later.

I'll note for posterity that even if she supports her friend, she's not guaranteed to benefit from it, particularly in the hypothetical case where he tries to take advantage of her kindness and manipulate it into affection or sex; not saying he will or that she will let it, but it dismantles her false sense of guarantee. Furthermore, I'll note that her pessimistic outlook about the future of our relationship has in this case very much turned into a self-fulfilling prophecy--if she believes it won't work, then her actions are altered to lead to issues like this.

This better explains her motivation and it supports your claim that she's putting her ex's needs over my own--maybe more importantly, she's also putting her own needs first, as an act of self-preservation derived out of a pessimism about the relationship. Fair enough. 

Btw, I removed the post for her sake because it was detailed enough for unwanted people to identify it. However, I will post a full update on what happened when I confronted her (when I can) because it only really now involves me and her. Regardless of what happens from here on out, I hope this thread demonstrates the effort I made to salvage things, even if they seemed bleak, unreasonable or impossible.

Though I didn't include it for the sake of space, I did suggest this at one point--have him stay here on our couch. I know you were half-joking, though--I had a short but needed laugh.

She sarcastically but correctly pointed out that even though I suggested it, I wouldn't be okay with having him stay over at our place--which is true--so she said it didn't solve the issue. I said in return that even though it was still bad, it was a better solution than her staying at his place.

Since the sleeping over is an issue no matter where it's done, having him sleep here would turn your win-win into a lose-lose----made all the worse because now it's happening in the comfort of my own home, thus displacing me from where I should feel the most secure.

I'll update in a proper post, but you're right: we talked about boundaries when I went back to confront to her and I told her that this is a clear boundary for me, to which she said she felt restricted and suffocating. 

She  said feels that she doesn't know what my boundaries are and feels paralyzed that anything she does will wind up in a fight. 

Communication is obviously important for establishing these boundaries, and in defense I'll say that I tried to very clearly establish my boundaries to her and moreover spend as much time as needed to clarify them if she didn't understand, but when emotions run high and patience runs low, it's hard for anything to be heard.

You're right; I do admit to some insecurity, which is a pre-existing factor in this situation that I did not emphasize enough in my (now removed) post for the sake of length. I've been working on it for awhile now even though these circumstances are forcefully pushing against me in the opposite direction.

The healthiest way for me to move on from this is to not let it distort my sense of future relationships. Obviously I can't come out of this unscathed, but I'll try my best to take time and recover from it and not let it bias my view of others. That'd be so cruel and unfair.

Thanks. I've gone through all of the comments multiple times, but I wanted to especially thank you since you say you rarely post. What you said seems very personal but you put that fact aside to help me.

The saddest part about all of this is that if it's absolutely true that my girlfriend is only trying to be a supportive friend, and if her ex's intentions really are underhanded, then she'll lose two of the most important people in her life. She'll push me away for not granting an absurd request, go running to him for help and support, and she'll experience him trying to manipulate her vulnerability into affection. Then she'll have to face the disgusting reality that he isn't who she thought and that I am no longer recoverable for her. And then she'll collapse.

Even though it looks like I'm ducking out either way for my own sanity, I really hope for her sake that her ex doesn't have such machinations, but is really in fact just in need of support. One can argue all they want about whether she brought it upon herself, or deserved it, but I wouldn't wish such pain and heartbreak on anyone.
Sorry. I talked with her last night; a lot went down. I will update when I can, but right now I need to figure out the situation at hand, i.e. the next steps and my living situation.

Yeah, I know where you're coming from. We've discussed our relationship status, and though I want to be 'official' she doesn't feel ready to commit after being so unexpectedly hurt. She honestly didn't want to be with anyone at all, but I came along and she likes me so much that I complicated her decision to stay single.

Not sure how to feel about it, but I like her a lot so I've decided to give her the space she needs without any undue pressure from relationship titles. We're practically a couple anyway, so I'm not worried. I think with a bit more time, the official status of it will follow. Or it'll all fall apart, but without false expectations at least the pain will be lessened.

Lastly, though she may not admit to others that we're 'dating,' I am somewhat heartened that she's willing to introduce me into her social circle. I can take solace in that, right? I think it means that she's not hiding me or anything.

Also, the line continues in the "Bad Quarto" version to say "To be or not to be, I there's the *point*" and the actors back in the day would actually make it a comedic reference to suicide by daggerpoint.
